Subject: Next steps: Hosting implications for EU/APAC residency and deployment modes

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on what hosting mode makes the most sense for EdgeHealth: hosted API (Redwood-hosted), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in EU), or Private (VPC / on-prem).

Key takeaways from our conversation:
- EdgeHealth requires EU data residency for PHI-derived telemetry and wants to understand cross-border routing for APAC pilot regions.
- Security team will require encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS, audit logs retention for 7 years, and an initial questionnaire for SOC 2 artifacts.
- Latency targets for EU users: p95 <= 180ms for short chat prompts; APAC pilot can tolerate higher latency if routed to Singapore.

What I’m attaching: a short one-pager comparing hosting modes and an initial SOW template (attached).

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether the requirement is strictly EU-only for all production data, or EU-only for PHI with non-PHI allowed in APAC test regions? (This will drive whether Hosted in EU suffices or if Private is needed.)
2) Ben will follow up with a brief note on Dedicated capacity sizing and latency tradeoffs.
3) If the security team is available, can they send their SOC 2 / KMS requirements by EOD Thursday so we can validate feasibility?
4) I’ll schedule a 30-min technical follow-up with Ben and Monica (our solutions engineer) — propose Wed 12/2 09:00 CET.

Thanks — we want to make sure the chosen path balances compliance and cost.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the succinct recap and the docs. A few clarifications from our side:
- For production PHI-derived data (EHR hashes, deidentified transcripts): EU-only is required — must reside in EU and never leave EU control.
- For non-PHI telemetry and the APAC pilot, we can accept hosting in APAC region (Singapore) but only for staging/pilot traffic; production analytics for EU patients must remain in EU.
- Security will send over the SOC 2 questionnaire and a KMS integration checklist by tomorrow morning.

Given that, we are primarily deciding between Dedicated capacity in an EU region vs Private VPC hosted in our Azure tenant. Our concerns:
- If Redwood Hosted (EU region) provides a certification-level isolation + customer KMS and granular audit logs, can that meet our compliance team? Or do they require a customer-managed VPC/tenant?
- What are the billing/commit/resizing implications for Dedicated vs Private? We want to avoid long-term overcommitment but need predictable throughput for Q1.

Appreciate the proposed time — Wed 12/2 09:00 CET works for Ben & me. I’ve added Security on the thread.

Best,
Jane Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeHealth Systems

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Next steps: Hosting implications for EU/APAC residency and deployment modes

Hi Jane —

Quick technical note ahead of the call:

1) Redwood Hosted (EU region) can support the compliance controls you listed: data residency by region, encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS (we integrate with Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS / GCP KMS), and per-tenant audit logs with configurable retention. For many customers this satisfies EU residency requirements without Private deployment.

2) The difference with Private (VPC/on-prem) is stronger tenant isolation and customer-managed network boundaries:
- Private VPC: customer deploys the inference runtime into their VPC (we ship an image + orchestration). Logs and telemetry can be retained in your storage account and we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Latency is typically lower for in-region traffic but ops responsibility is higher for your infra team.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools we manage in our cloud but dedicated to your org. This gives predictable throughput and SLAs while keeping operational overhead with Redwood. It sits between Hosted and Private on the isolation spectrum.

3) Cost/commit guidance:
- Hosted: pay-as-you-go; best for pilots but unit-tokens cost is higher.
- Dedicated: monthly commit with burst options; good if you can estimate Q1 throughput. We can do quarterly lookback adjustments in the SOW.
- Private: licensing + infra costs; recommended if legal requires customer-controlled tenancy or specific network egress control.

4) Cross-region routing: we support policy-based routing so PHI traffic can be pinned to EU endpoints while pilot traffic from APAC is routed to SG endpoints. If you need strict EU-only for any data class, Hosted EU (with KMS + audit logs) or Private VPC are both viable — choice depends on legal stance on managed tenancy.

I’ll cover sizing options and latency tradeoffs on the call. Monica will pull a sample SOW addendum for Dedicated + Private cost comparators.

—Ben
